correctness.rationale: For \(m\ge3\), \(q\ge1\), the exact invariant-spectrum decomposition gives the transverse two-by-two block \(M(a,b)\) and the uniform/leaf-difference modes. The fixed positive vector \( (1,\sqrt q(1+s)) \) proves \(\mu\ge1-s^2/[1+q(1+s)^2]\) for every invariant feasible chain; convex group averaging transfers this lower bound to all symmetric stochastic matrices on the graph. At \(a=s(1+s)/T\), \(b=(1-qa)/(m-1)\), the vector is an exact top eigenvector; trace and scalar inequalities bound all other modes. Equality forces b maximal and uniquely determines a within the invariant class. The edge-ordering identity and limits are algebraic. Symbolic identities and 49 full matrices/294 competitors passed in the attached verifier; finite tests are supporting, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Clique-corona networks model dense backbone communication with local pendant bottlenecks, and their exact optimal stochastic averaging rate is a natural two-parameter graph-design invariant. The theorem gives a global optimum over all symmetric chains, a constructive unique invariant design, a positive dual Rayleigh witness, mandatory zero holding on cores, a sharp transition at \(q=m-1\) between optimal core versus pendant edge weights, and two scaling limits. These solve the precise spectral allocation problem rather than recomputing a known graph spectrum.
